errors: The equivalence (i)+(ii) ⇔ (iii) is false for an arbitrary cofibrantly generated weak factorization system; it needs extra hypotheses, which the marginal 'under suitable assumptions' acknowledges. A standard sufficient set: C = monomorphisms of the topos (so C is automatically stable under pushout-products), all objects cofibrant, and 2-out-of-3 for W. Under these, TC stable under ×Z gives the pushout-product condition by a 2-of-3 argument.
TC = C ∩ W̃ uses that TC is closed under retracts. This is automatic if TC is defined (or saturated) by a lifting property, but not if TC is merely 'generated' in a weaker sense; this is not stated.

ideas.what: Compatibility with internal Hom: α(i,f) is a fibration, trivial if i or f is trivial; equivalence with stability of C, TC under ×Z and of F, TF under Hom(Z,−)
ideas.modern_name: Pushout-product axiom / SM7 / cartesian (closed) model category; Joyal–Tierney–Cisinski criterion for cartesian model structures on toposes
ideas.usually_credited_to: Quillen (SM7, 1967); Hovey (monoidal model categories, 1999); Joyal–Tierney and Cisinski for the topos criterion
ideas.where_published: Not, to my knowledge, in Pursuing Stacks in this form

missed.claim: As early as June 1982, before Pursuing Stacks, Grothendieck was setting up model structures on a topos generated by a set of trivial cofibrations, together with the cartesian-closedness criterion '(i) TC stable under ×Z ⇔ (iii) pullback-hom condition'. This prefigures the Cisinski / Joyal–Tierney criterion for cartesian model structures on presheaf toposes. It is a historical precedent rather than a new mathematical result.
missed.quote: (i) C, TC stable by cartesian products ? × Z ... (iii) If i ∈ C, f ∈ F, then α(i,f) ∈ F, and if moreover i ∈ TC or f ∈ TF, then α(i,f) ∈ TF.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents Grothendieck's pre-1983 engagement with Quillen model structures on toposes. This is relevant to the historiography of Cisinski's theory and of cartesian model structures, which are usually traced to Pursuing Stacks plus later work by Joyal and Cisinski.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is standard model-category bookkeeping: the retract argument and the SM7/pushout-product equivalence. The modest interest lies in the date (1982, pre-Pursuing Stacks) and the explicit topos/cartesian setting, which anticipates Cisinski-style results.
transcription_corrections: 'W̃ = Fl(W)' is more plausibly 'W̃ ⊂ Fl(A)' (arrows of the topos A), with the set-builder below it. The NB says W has not yet been used, which fits this reading.
'not plus TC ⊂ C' should read 'nor TC ⊂ C'.
'by {+generated by+} (TC)_0 ⊂ C_0' should read roughly 'the way they were obtained (generated) by (TC)_0 ⊂ C_0'.
'of [-fini-] small [?] ... sums' is probably 'of [-finite-] small sums (direct limits?) and fibered products'.
The marginal note near (iii) reads 'under suitable assumptions'; it attaches to the double arrow ⇕ between (i)+(ii) and (iii).
The crossed-out opening reads 'c) X→Y is ∈ W', and the page header '2' is a sub-page number.
